title: Ignorance & Suffering
description: Identify the root causes of mental suffering and learn the tools to overcome ignorance, ego, and attachment for lasting peace.

sutra.meaning: Suffering comes from 1. ignorance or lack of wisdom, 2.ego, 3.attachment to pleasure, 4.aversion to pain and 5.fear of death. These are the root causes of disturbance in our equilibrium.
sutra.padaVibhaga: avidyā | asmitā | rāga | dveṣa | abhiniveśāḥ | kleśāḥ
sutra.wordMeanings: avidyā = ignorance; asmitā = ego; rāga = attraction; dveṣa = aversion; abhiniveśāḥ = clinging to life; kleśāḥ = afflictions

sections.insight: All sufferings have one or the other of these at its root.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I see their presence in me
sections.practice: Recall incidents causing you distress and identify the reason at their root
sections.shlokaFrom: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः॥ 4.40
sections.wisdomFrom: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting soul are destroyed. There is neither this world nor the next, nor happiness for the doubting soul.

sutra.meaning: Spiritual ignorance is the root of all suffering because it may cause arrogance, cravings, aversion, attachment etc which are impediments to growth and cause suffering.
sutra.padaVibhaga: avidyā | kṣetram | uttareṣām | prasupta | tanu | vicchinna | udārāṇām
sutra.wordMeanings: avidyā = ignorance; kṣetram = field; uttareṣām = of the following; prasupta = dormant; tanu = attenuated; vicchinna = interrupted; udārāṇām = fully active

sections.insight: Unawareness fuels all reactions which cause karmic residue.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I  function unawares of the cause or consequence?
sections.shlokaFrom: तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः।छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत॥ 4.42
sections.wisdomFrom: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut asunder this doubt in your heart born of ignorance. Take refuge in yoga and arise, O Bharata!
sections.gurudevInsight: Ignorance is holding on to the past. Holding on to this, to that. Having an idea of who you are. People think that it is a very complimentary sentence to know who you are and having an idea of who you are. I tell you, if you have an idea of who you are you are gone, finished, you are stuck. You do not know who you are, that should be the right attitude. You are changing every moment and you have kept the possibility of change open. A fixed idea about who you are destroys you totally. It stops your growth and brings a limit to your possibilities.

sections.theme: We mistake the temporary for truth.

sutra.meaning: Confusing temporary as permanent is ignorance for example assuming the world to be prmanent.
sutra.padaVibhaga: anitya | aśuci | duḥkha | anātmasu | nitya | śuci | sukha | ātma | khyātiḥ | avidyā
sutra.wordMeanings: anitya = impermanent; aśuci = impure; duḥkha = painful; anātmasu = non-self; nitya = permanent; śuci = pure; sukha = pleasant; ātma = Self; khyātiḥ = knowing as; avidyā = ignorance

sections.insight: Misperception of what really matters creates suffering.Misperception creates suffering. Life itself is impermanent so everything else around it too is not permanent.
sections.reflectionPrompt: What am I holding as permanent which is perishable?
sections.shlokaFrom: यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति।तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम्॥ 7.21
sections.wisdomFrom: Whatever form any devotee desires to worship with faith, I make that faith of his steady.
sections.gurudevInsight: Ignorance is the root cause of suffering.  You think that which is not permanent as permanent. You think that,which is changing as not changing. That which is not joy as joy, which is not self as the self. I am not the body but thinking that “I am the body”. I am not the thoughts or emotions, but thinking that “I am my thoughts and emotions”.You feel that the body is not changing, but the body is changing all the time. Everyday your body is changing. In 24 hours the blood changes. In five days the lining of the stomach changes. Doctors say that in a whole month the skin changes.In a year every cell in the body changes. You never thought or understood that your body is like a river. It is undergoing change all the time. Your body has completely different cells in one year.

sections.theme: The ego is a case of mistaken identity.

sutra.meaning: Ego is identification of seer with seeing ie the body, mind and intellect as the eternal, indestructible Self
sutra.padaVibhaga: dṛk | darśana | śaktyoḥ | ekātmatā | iva | asmitā
sutra.wordMeanings: dṛk = the Seer; darśana = seeing; śaktyoḥ = of the powers; ekātmatā = oneness; iva = as if; asmitā = ego/I-am-ness

sections.insight: We confuse self with the roles we are playing.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Who am I beyond the roles?
sections.gurudevInsight: Asmita is oneness of the intellect and ourself. Have noticed that in a meeting some people say a point and stick to that point? They are totally stuck to that point. Most of the people go on arguing and arguing meaninglessly and it leads to senseless argument. This senseless argument comes because they are so stuck and think their intellect as themselves, their thoughts as themselves. “My thought, my opinion, me, me”, inability to see the self and the buddhi or the intellect and the instruments of perception as separate. This is asmita.

sections.theme: Craving is the trap of pleasure.

sutra.meaning: "Attraction to pleasant experience results in craving."
sutra.wordMeanings: sukha = pleasure; anuśayī = following/dwelling on; rāgaḥ = attachment/desire

sections.insight: When we experience pleasure, we develop a longing for it. This creates a craving or desire to repeat the experience, which binds the mind and causes suffering when the pleasure ends.
sections.practice: Honestly think about your feelings in this respect.
sections.gurudevInsight: This craving makes you miserable. Patanjali says that there are only five sources of misery. There is no sixth source of misery. Ignorance, or thinking that which is changing as non-changing. We try to control others mind saying that they should be this way, that way. How is it possible? Someone may have had love for you yesterday, but not today, or tomorrow, who knows? They themselves do not know. Do you see that? We expect an enlightened behavior from everybody around us. Then we become unhappy. You are not behaving in an enlightened way, but you expect everybody else to behave in an enlightened way and to give unconditional love. You want them to give you unconditional love. When you expect this from people all around you, that is where you become unhappy.

sections.theme: Aversion is the shadow of pain.

sutra.wordMeanings: duḥkha = pain; anuśayī = following; dveṣaḥ = aversion/hatred

sections.insight: When we experience pain or unpleasantness, we develop a strong dislike or avoidance of it. This emotional reaction (anger, fear, or resentment) causes suffering.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Does even a little hardship derail me?
sections.practice: Honestly think about your feelings in this respect.
sections.gurudevInsight: Hatred comes, aversion comes with an unpleasant experience. Aversion also brings the same misery as happiness brings misery. Craving and aversion are both sources of misery. Abhinivesha or fear, fear of unknown. Though intellectually everything is know, even in great scholars there is a little amount of abhinivesha. Nature has enforced all these five things in everybody. Now, how thin can this get or how thick can this get? It can either make you evolve or unevolved.

sutra.meaning: "Fear flowing in its own flavour even in the wise is established in them as carefulness."
sutra.padaVibhaga: svarasavāhī | viduṣaḥ | api | tathā | ārūḍhaḥ | abhiniveśaḥ
sutra.wordMeanings: svarasavāhī = self-sustaining; viduṣaḥ = of the wise; api = even; tathā = so; ārūḍhaḥ = established; abhiniveśaḥ = clinging to life/fear of death

sections.insight: The deep-rooted will to survive (or fear of death/clinging to life) persists even among the wiseThis is the subtlest klesha, representing the instinctual fear of death and the desire to stay alive at any cost. Patanjali notes that this urge is so powerful it affects everyone, including those who are knowledgeable..
sections.reflectionPrompt: How fearful am I? Am I always fearful of impending doom. Am I ready to handle all situations?
sections.practice: sit quietly and imagine yourself dying. What feelings are arising. Observe
sections.gurudevInsight: It should not even be called as fear. It should be called as alertness. Fear has a different meaning altogether. It is a mix of alertness, carefulness and fear.Abhinivesha in its thickest form is fear and in its thinnest form, in its diluted form is care. You are walking on the edge of the lake and you are putting your steps carefully so that you will not fall into the water. If this care would not have been there then this body would have vanished, disappeared. "When I am not the body, I will not attend to the body at all". In that case, "I will not have the body to speak longer or to do anything". To maintain the body certain amount of care is essential. Is this clear? When this care becomes little more than what is needed, then it becomes insecurity. If it becomes more, a little more, it is being paranoid. It is just like salt. If salt becomes more it becomes impossible to eat it.

sections.theme: The wise see suffering in all change.

sutra.transliteration: pariṇāma-tāpa-saṁskāra-duḥkhair guṇa-vṛtti-virodhāc ca duḥkham eva sarvaṁ vivekinaḥ
sutra.meaning: Wise see suffering in all change, even what apparently seems pleasant is tinged with suffering and sorrow.
sutra.padaVibhaga: pariṇāma | tāpa | saṁskāra | duḥkhaiḥ | guṇa | vṛtti | virodhāt | ca | duḥkham | eva | sarvam | vivekinaḥ
sutra.wordMeanings: pariṇāma = change; tāpa = affliction; saṁskāra = impressions; duḥkhaiḥ = by sufferings; guṇa = qualities; vṛtti = fluctuations; virodhāt = due to conflict; ca = and; duḥkham = suffering; eva = indeed; sarvam = all; vivekinaḥ = of the discerning

sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I accept change without getting derailed?
sections.practice: Observe impermanence in all things around you
sections.gurudevInsight:
"-every event causes some pain. However an event is
pleasant, because an event finishes, ends so the ending of an event however pleasurable,
joyful has been, comes to you with a little pinch, pain. Greater the joy, greater the pain also,
isn’t it? Parinaam dukha – Effect of, result of any event leaves you in pain. Paap Dukha –
Longing for an event, waiting for a pleasurable pleasant event is again pain. Sanskara Dukha
– The Impressions of it, memories of it memories of pleasure also brings pain. Before you
want something, that wanting, that feverishness to achieve what you want is all painful.
When you have it, the fear of losing it is painful, when it is gone; the memory of its joy is
painful. So the whole thing is all painful. For a viveki, for an intelligent person, for one
whose wisdom is awakened, he sees the whole thing, as pain. So there is nothing that is not
pain."

sutra.meaning: Future suffering can be avoided if we adopt the path of yoga because this alone prevents further impressions ie. karma from taking root.
sutra.wordMeanings: heyam = to be avoided; duḥkham = suffering; anāgatam = yet to come/future

sections.insight: Awareness of the impermanency of the world prevents future suffering.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I established on the path of yoga?
sections.gurudevInsight:
When you realize that everything is pain, then how do you go ahead about,
what you do? You have to do something to stop this pain. How will you do it? The root
cause of pain is needed to be eliminated, we need to eliminate the dukham. That pain which
has not yet come in life, that sorrow which has not yet sprouted should be nipped off right at
the beginning.

sections.theme: The seer is not the seen.

sutra.meaning: Union of seer and seen causes suffering because the self which is eternal is mistakenly seen as the same as the body with its organs of perception etc
sutra.wordMeanings: draṣṭṛ = Seer; dṛśyayoḥ = seen; saṁyogaḥ = union; heya-hetuḥ = cause of what is to be avoided

sections.insight: Attachment to the non permanent causes confusion.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I differentiate between my body and the Self yet?
sections.practice: Observe separation of seer and seen
sections.shlokaFrom: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्।स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा॥ 6.23
sections.wisdomFrom: Know that severance from union with pain is called yoga. This yoga should be practiced with determination and with an undaunted mind.
sections.gurudevInsight: Forgetfulness of one’s self as separate from one’s environment is the main cause of suffering.Life is not in oneself. Life is somewhere else, in the bank account. You have not just deposited  the money in the bank. Along with the money, you have deposited your life also. If something happens to the bank account, you have a heart failure. Do you see what I am saying? Whatever you think as more important, be it matter or material, you give more importance to it than the life. That becomes the cause of suffering. So when you see the difference, then the seer, the light, separates from the surrounding and then you see, “what is all this?” Then, true meditation happens.

sections.theme: Kriya yoga is the path through.

sutra.sanskrit: तदभावात् संयोगाभावो हानं तद् दृशेः कैवल्यम्
sutra.meaning: One must practice the kriya discipline because it affords a sadhak the tools whereby the perceiver is separated from the perceived.
sutra.padaVibhaga: tat | abhāvāt | saṁyoga | abhāvaḥ | hānam | tat | dṛśeḥ | kaivalyam
sutra.wordMeanings: tat = that (ignorance); abhāvāt = from absence; saṁyoga = union; abhāvaḥ = absence; hānam = removal; tat = that; dṛśeḥ = of the Seer; kaivalyam = liberation

sections.insight: Right knowledge is a necessity on the path of yoga if the practitioner has to break the link between the seer and the seen and get self-realisation.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I have confidence in my path and the determination to follow it.
sections.practice: Practice observing separation of seer and seen
sections.journalPrompt: Did I feel the separation during meditation.
